description:
Found by the Bugs and Cleanup session while proposing fz-3sy.35; filed as decision B on ../fz-3sy.35.html (approved by the user 2026-11-17).

Elixir refuses an undefined variable or %Nope{} in a function nothing calls, and warns about Nope.go(1). fz says nothing about any of them. Repro:
  def f(), do: undefined_var
  def main(), do: IO.inspect(1)
exits 0 under fz; Elixir fails to compile.

fz-3sy.35 checks unreached declarations (@spec/@type/extern) only; this is about unreached bodies. Fixing it means expanding and scoping unreached bodies, which costs more than checking declarations, and meets fz-sc8.216 (executables nothing reaches are compiled anyway): the check must not lower or compile the body, only expand and scope it. Library bodies stay cold, as in fz-3sy.35 decision A.

Done when: the three cases (undefined variable, unknown struct, call to an undefined remote function) report as Elixir does on interp, run and build, pinned by fixtures; a drive test asserts the unreached function is expanded and scoped but never lowered.
title: A function nothing calls still has its body checked, as in Elixir
